subject: Clear Signal 001: Clients are asking ChatGPT who to hire
preheader: Make sure it can find you. Plus one prompt to try today and four quick hits. Five minutes.
hello: AI can feel like a lot. Clear Signal keeps it simple: one change worth knowing, one prompt you can use today, and a few quick hits. Five minutes, then back to your clients.

oneThing.title: Clients are asking ChatGPT who to hire

points.label: What it is
points.text: OpenAI now lets businesses claim a profile in ChatGPT, so when someone asks it for a local agent, advisor or office, your details come straight from you. It's a beta that started November 10.

points.label: Try this
points.text: Ask ChatGPT what a client would ask: "Who are good real estate agents in [your town]?" If you're missing or something's off, that's your sign to claim your profile.

points.label: The fine print
points.text: In the US, local businesses can claim an existing listing. You'll confirm you own or run the business with a photo ID, and changes are reviewed before they show.

field.question: "Is it safe to put client info into AI?"
field.answer: Treat a chat like a shared notepad, not a vault. Keep names, addresses and money details out unless your brokerage has approved the tool, and use a temporary chat for anything sensitive so it isn't saved.

quickHits.title: Talk, don't type
quickHits.text: Between showings, tap the microphone in the ChatGPT app and talk through a client follow-up. Then ask it to turn that into a short text you can send.

quickHits.title: Google Maps finds the appointment
quickHits.text: In the US, Ask Maps can now look for beauty, pet care, auto and home repair openings and call local businesses for you, and it plans day-by-day trips. Handy for clients moving to a new town.

quickHits.title: Spot mistakes in a bill
quickHits.text: Paste a phone or utility bill into ChatGPT and ask it to explain each charge, flag new or doubled fees, and write a short script for calling the company.

quickHits.title: Keep your logins to yourself
quickHits.text: Don't give an AI helper your bank or airline password. Some big companies now block AI assistants from signing in for you, and a slip can cost real money.
